title: 19-year-old with hours-long attacks of imbalance, vertigo and nausea

provenance.citation: Synthetic case written 2026-10-17 for Rare Disease Detective; not derived from any individual patient.

chief_complaint: "A few times a month I suddenly can't walk straight, the room spins and I throw up. It lasts most of the day."
history_of_present_illness: Since age 12, recurrent episodes of unsteadiness, slurred speech, vertigo and nausea lasting 2–12 hours, 2–4 times per month. Triggers he has noticed: emotional stress (exams), heavy exercise, and alcohol. Some episodes are followed by a throbbing headache. Between attacks he feels 'mostly fine' but admits to being 'a bit clumsy' on stairs in the dark for the past two years. No loss of consciousness, no hearing loss, no tinnitus. Caffeine seems to worsen attacks.

symptom_timeline.event: Attacks increase during exams; trialed propranolol without clear benefit
Persistent mild imbalance between attacks begins
ED visit during an attack; neurology referral

movement_findings.observation: Interictal: downbeat nystagmus in primary gaze, more evident on lateral and downgaze; gaze-evoked nystagmus bilaterally.
Interictal: mild truncal ataxia on tandem gait; normal limb coordination.
During attack (ED note, physician-documented): marked gait and limb ataxia, dysarthria, vomiting; no limb weakness.

imaging.report: Mild atrophy of the superior cerebellar vermis. Otherwise normal. No demyelination.

family_history: Mother has 'migraines with dizziness' since her teens. Maternal grandfather 'walked like he was drunk' in his 60s. No consanguinity.
social_history: Drinks 4–6 drinks on weekend nights; notes attacks often follow.
